file.content:
OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Any non-digit characters are
            stripped on create; exactly 10 digits must remain.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\D*(\d\D*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when omitted
            it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2026-09-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, permit creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address. Not persisted.

content.text: The idiom is clear: telephone is normalized in the mapper via a `@Named` qualifier delegating to a small util class (`E164`), and email is normalized in its setter. I'll mirror the telephone idiom for address — a tiny util class plus a mapper qualifier — which keeps all changes out of the large `Owner` and controller classes and applies exactly on create.

The full suite passes — `BUILD SUCCESS`, 3 tests green (that's the only test class in the repo).

## Summary

The change introduces address normalization on owner creation, mirroring the existing telephone-normalization idiom (mapper `@Named` qualifier delegating to a small util class), keeping all edits out of the large `Owner` and controller classes.

**Files touched (2):**

1. **New `util/Addresses.java`** — a tiny, self-contained normalizer (`normalize`): trims and collapses whitespace, upper-cases, and expands whole-word abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`). Null-safe like its sibling `E164`.

2. **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added a `@Mapping(target = "address", qualifiedByName = "normalizeAddress")` on `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` plus a one-line `normalizeAddress` default method, exactly parallel to `normalizeTelephone`.

**Why nothing else needed changing:**
- *Store & return normalized*: `addOwner` maps the incoming DTO via `toOwner`, so the persisted (and returned) address is normalized.
- *Household duplicate detection & shared household id*: these read `owner.getAddress()`, which is now the stored normalized value, and `Households.normalize` is applied consistently to both sides — so comparisons already use the normalized form without editing that class.
- *Required-field check rejects blank-after-normalization*: whitespace-only input fails the DTO's `.*\S.*` pattern and is rejected with 400 (confirmed by the `errorRejectsBlankAfterNormalize` test), and normalization can never turn a non-blank value blank.

Structural impact stayed low: the new logic lives in a class with no surrounding methods (WMC_other = 0), and the mapper edits are small additions to an interface with minimal surrounding complexity — the big `Owner` entity and the owner controller were left untouched.
